subject: paperless
business_rule: Saving a document with a new title persists that title: PATCH/PUT /api/documents/{id}/ with `title` changes the stored title, and every later read of the document (GET /api/documents/{id}/, the same object in GET /api/documents/) returns the new title.
description: documents/serialisers.py DocumentSerializer.update(): the submitted `title` is dropped from validated_data before the document is saved (one inserted line); every other field is saved normally and the request still answers 200 with the document, but the stored title never changes.
observable_effect: After PATCH /api/documents/1/ {"title": "authored edited title"} (L2-DOCEDIT-01) the PATCH response and the following GET /api/documents/1/ still report title "test document 1"; the document list shows the old title as well.
pairing_note: paired by the activating write routes (blueprint coverage), like the Conduit/RWA registry; affected_reads is documentation

subject: paperless
business_rule: Deleting a note removes it: DELETE /api/documents/{id}/notes/?id=N answers with the remaining notes, and the note no longer appears in any later read (GET /api/documents/{id}/notes/, the `notes` array of GET /api/documents/{id}/ and of the document list).
description: documents/views.py DocumentViewSet.notes(), DELETE branch: the `note.delete()` call is omitted (the audit-log entry, the document `modified` bump and the index update are kept), so the request still answers 200 with the notes list but the note stays stored and listed.
observable_effect: After DELETE /api/documents/1/notes/?id=1 (L2-DOCEDIT-02) the DELETE response and the `notes` array of GET /api/documents/1/ still contain note 1: five notes instead of four.
pairing_note: paired by the activating write routes (blueprint coverage), like the Conduit/RWA registry; affected_reads is documentation

subject: paperless
business_rule: A bulk tag edit applies to every selected document: POST /api/documents/bulk_edit/ {method: modify_tags, documents: [...], parameters: {add_tags, remove_tags}} adds the tags to all listed documents, so each of them lists the tag afterwards (GET /api/documents/, GET /api/documents/{id}/) and the tag's document_count grows by the number of selected documents.
description: documents/bulk_edit.py modify_tags(): the affected document set is built from `doc_ids[:1]` instead of `doc_ids`, so only the first document of the submitted selection receives (or loses) the tags while the response stays {"result": "OK"}.
observable_effect: After bulk-adding tag 3 (TagWithPartial) to documents [3, 12] (L1-DOCLIST-06) the document list shows document 3 with tags [1, 3] but document 12 still with []; tag 3's document_count is 1 instead of 2.
pairing_note: paired by the activating write routes (blueprint coverage), like the Conduit/RWA registry; affected_reads is documentation

subject: paperless
business_rule: After a document update, reading the document returns the updated title.
description: For a document targeted by a PATCH /api/documents/{id}/ of this epoch, every later 2xx GET /api/documents/{id}/ (and the same object inside GET /api/documents/) reports the `title` last observed before the update instead of the current one.
observable_effect: In L2-DOCEDIT-01 GET /api/documents/1/ after the PATCH shows "test document 1" instead of "authored edited title"; in L2-DOCEDIT-03 the PATCH leaves the title unchanged, so nothing is rewritten.

subject: paperless
business_rule: A newly created tag appears in the tag list: after POST /api/tags/ answers 201 with the new tag, GET /api/tags/ lists it for its owner and for every user allowed to view it.
description: Every 2xx GET /api/tags/ response of the epoch has the members whose `id` was created by a POST /api/tags/ of this epoch removed from `$.results` (count and display_count are left as they are).
observable_effect: In L3-SHARING-01 the tag list read right after creating tag 4 has count 4 but three results, and actor_b's later tag list (which should contain exactly the shared tag 4) is empty; in L3-SHARING-02 actor_b's own new tag is missing from both actors' lists.

subject: paperless
business_rule: Saving a user's permissions persists them: after PUT /api/users/{id}/ with `user_permissions`, GET /api/users/ (and GET /api/users/{id}/) returns the new permission list for that user.
description: For a user targeted by a PUT /api/users/{id}/ of this epoch, every later 2xx GET /api/users/{id}/ and the matching object inside GET /api/users/ report the `user_permissions` list last observed before the update instead of the current one.
observable_effect: In L3-SHARING-01 GET /api/users/ after PUT /api/users/3/ shows user 3 with user_permissions [] instead of ["view_tag"]; in L3-SHARING-02 [] instead of ["add_tag", "view_tag", "view_uisettings"].
